scope: Two independent issuers; signed public identity PushDrop outputs; two malicious lookup response records whose output transactions remain consensus-valid; public trust settings with exact restoration; actual spent revocation token and local relinquishment. Native restart and permission predicates require actual browser/UI receipts. Reference executions cannot satisfy those predicates.
interpretation: Discovery rejection must filter the malformed certificate while preserving both independently authenticated valid controls. A lookup-service response is not proof of overlay admission. Permission default semantics are tested only after an explicit true/deny call establishes that permission is required for that fresh origin. Revocation does not invalidate the issuer signature or imply unspecified proof/discovery revocation policy.
